Definition: from G575 and a derivative of G245; to estrange away, i.e. (passively and figuratively) to be non-participant:-- alienate, be alien.
BiblicalUsage: To estrange, to alienate, to make a stranger of. Paul says the Gentiles were aliens from the commonwealth of Israel and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope and without God, and that the understanding is darkened and men are alienated from the life of God through ignorance. The word names the distance sin puts between man and God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe alienation is the truest name for what sin did: it made strangers of us, far from the covenants and without hope in the world. Paul says we were alienated from the life of God, and I hold that the gospel is the end of that estrangement, Christ bringing near those who were far off.
